title: Hunting Seasons File (Jagdzeiten)
description: Shared shape for the federal base layer (data/federal.json) and per-state delta files (data/states/*.json). Effective seasons = mergeSeasons(federal, state, taxonomy) — see src/lib/seasons.ts. Every season's `key` references data/taxonomy.json; verbatim regulation wording lives in `notes`. State files carry ONLY deviations from the federal defaults.

state.description: Two-letter German state code (state files only)

name.description: Full name of the federal state (state files only)

source.description: Provenance for citation. Not authoritative legal advice.

key.description: Universal match key: a taxonomy speciesKey, optionally with a /classKey suffix (e.g. 'reh/ricke', 'fuchs/jung', 'dachs'). A bare speciesKey for a species the taxonomy splits is expanded to its class atoms at merge time.

type.description: range = open during the listed periods; year-round = huntable all year (ganzjährig); closed = no open season (ganzjährige Schonzeit). Permit-only hunting (e.g. Fischotter/Wolf in Bavaria) is type 'range'|'closed' with conditional:true and empty periods.

periods.description: Open date ranges. Omitted/empty for year-round, closed, and permit-only. A period wraps the year boundary when end < start.

end.description: MM-DD inclusive. '02-28' denotes end of February per the regulation wording.

conditional.description: true if hunting is permitted only under legal restrictions (Vergrämung/Schadensabwehr, spatial limits, or an individual Ausnahme/Befreiung). The traffic-light UI must show this distinctly from a plain open season.

provenance.description: Set by mergeSeasons on the effective output; not stored in source files.

notes.description: Verbatim regulation wording and caveats (the verbatim species/class names live here as flavour)

term.description: State-local term for this entry's class, overriding the canonical taxonomy label in the per-state view (e.g. Bavaria's 'Geißen' for 'reh/ricke' vs the federal 'Ricken'). Only meaningful on class-level keys.
